title: Spelling Teams: ea
goal: I can spell long e words with the ea team, like read and beach.

card.desc: Bristol meets vowel teams: two vowels that make one sound. The ea team usually says long e (eat, read, beach, clean, dream, team). A few ea words say short e (head, bread), so she learns to try long e first. It works on her old mistake of writing red for read.

win: Great spelling! The ea team is on your side!

teacher.objective: Bristol learns that a vowel team is two vowels that make one sound, and that ea usually says long e (eat, read, beach, clean, dream, team). She learns that a few ea words say short e (head, bread) and reads new ea words by trying long e first. She tells long e (ea) from short e (e) in pairs like red / read and net / neat, which fixes her red-for-read spelling. Week 7 Day 1 (Learn it).
materials: Zoom with screen share (open the Class lesson from the course page, code 9110)
At her home: paper, pencil, a marker, 2 sticky notes (or small squares of paper), her book
Your whiteboard (or paper held to the camera)
Packet (2 pages) for Tia to print this week (it is due Thursday, on Tuesday's task list)

plan.do: Class slide 1. Share your screen. Check her paper, marker, sticky notes and book.
Class slide 2. What happened; she reads one sentence; an ea word from her book.
Class slide 3. won't and a 6s fact. She answers; you type and tap.
Class slide 4. Long e says its name; short e is the sound in bed.
Class slide 5. Six words; she reads, stretches and spells each one.
Class slide 6. She writes both and holds them up.
Class slide 7. Long e → ea, short e → e.
Class slide 8. Try long e first.
Class slide 9. She reads each word and names the box; you tap.
Class slide 10. She reads every choice before she picks.
Class slide 11. An ea sticky note in s_t, h_t, n_t; then just e.
Class slides 12–13. She spells out loud; you type exactly what she says.
Class slide 14. Two ea words from her book.
Class slide 16. Show tonight's task list: the After-Class Lesson and 10 minutes of reading. Nothing else.

watch: red for read (her own mistake). Ask: "Is it a color, or something you do with a book?"
Writing only e for a long e sound (bech, clen, lef). Ask: "Long e or short e? Long e needs the team."
Writing the team backward (ae: baech, claen). The e comes first, and the e does the talking.
Reading head or bread with long e. Remind her: try long e first; if it does not make sense, try short e.
Writing ee for an ea word (meet for meat, reed for read). Both teams say long e, so this is a memory word. Say which word it is (meet a friend vs. meat to eat). We do not test ee this week.
ea words with r (year, near, learn) or long a (great, break) if she finds them in her book. Tell her they are different and we learn them later.

packet_key.answer: Any 2 ea words from her book, spelled right, with the ea circled.

teacher.notes: Tonight is light on purpose: only the After-Class Lesson (it ends with Show What You Know, 3 sets that rotate on retakes) and 10 minutes of reading. This lesson's Practice and Packet are on Tuesday's task list, due Thursday. Check her score before Tuesday. If she scores under 85, start Lesson 17 with 5 minutes of ea sticky notes (seat/set, neat/net, read/red) and have her retake Show What You Know (new set) before the Lesson 17 After-Class Lesson. Use read only in the now sense this week (I like to read). Do not test ee spellings yet.

slides.title: What is a vowel team?
slides.text: A vowel team is two vowels side by side that make one sound.

steps.text: In eat, the e and the a are a team.
Together they say long e. Long e says its name: E.
Short e is different. It is the sound in bed.

slides.tip: The e does the talking. The a is quiet.

slides.title: ea hunt in your book
slides.text: Look in your book for words with ea.
prompts: Read each one. Does the ea say long e or short e?

notes.do: About 4 minutes. She hunts and holds up the page.
notes.listen: Most will be long e (each, please, eat). If she finds great or break, say: "Wow, that one is a rule-breaker. It says long a! There are only a few like that." If she finds an ea with r (year, near, learn), say: "The r changes the sound. We will learn those later."
